_criterion_assessments_for_d.chunk_text:
4.3 Tasks/Routines/Functions
The analog inputs and outputs will be scaled with MapIn and MapOut routines as described
according to the MCCPDC Controller Guidelines document and using the values in the
MCCPDC Alarms Hard Soft IO Listing.xlsx.
For this work the following specific routines are expected:
R105_EMS
R110_MapInLAD
R111_MapInFBD
R120_MapOutLAD
R121_MapOutFBD
4.4 Operator Interface
Each of the EMS input signals is displayed in engineering units on the HMI. As mentioned
previously, with the proper credentials, the input points can be simulated for calibration or other
maintenance activities. Similarly, given the proper credentials, the alarm limits for the EMS
signals are also available for review and adjustment via the HMI.
The visual and audible annunciators (light trees and audible alerts) also provide feedback to
personnel in the area without the need to actively view an HMI screen.
4.5 Messages and Alarming
The EMS messages and alarms, together with other system alarms, are described in the overall
PCS system document named MCCPDC PCS-CP01 Alarms Hard Soft IO Listing.xlsx. That
document provides, among other details, the alarm text, the input point tag identifier, the alarm
setpoint, and any time-delay associated with the alarm. For the alarms listed here, alarm limit
processing, time delay, etc. is handled in the PLC and not in the FactoryTalk Alarm and Events
Server.
The alarm setpoints are not calculated but are static, user-adjustable values via the HMI as
detailed in the MCCPDC PCS-CP01 Alarms Hard Soft IO Listing.xlsx document.
See Section 4.1.6.1 Alarms/Beacons to see the description of acknowledging and resetting of
alarms.
